subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Block and Tackle: Multiplying Force with Rope
description: A quick, practical guide to Block and Tackle: Multiplying Force with Rope.

hook.text: A block and tackle with four pulleys lets one person lift 400 kilograms with just 100 kilograms of pull.

buildup.text: Multiple pulleys share the load across more rope segments. More pulleys means less force per pull.

discovery.text: The mechanical advantage equals the number of rope segments supporting the load. Four segments, four times easier.

twist.text: But you pull four times more rope. Lifting a load one meter requires pulling four meters of rope.

climax.text: Construction cranes use block and tackle systems. So do elevators, sailboats, and rescue teams.

punchline.text: Add pulleys, subtract effort. Physics always balances the books.

quiz.question: In a block and tackle, what determines the mechanical advantage?
options: The total weight of the pulleys in the system
The number of rope segments supporting the load
The diameter of the largest pulley in the system
